subject: ventures/wage-garnishment-limit-calculator
professional: a payroll compliance specialist who processes garnishment orders; first checks: disposable earnings counts only deductions required by law; the 25%-or-30x-floor rule and its pay-period multiples (Fact Sheet #30); support percentages 50/55/60/65; how a support order already being withheld reduces room for a later creditor or student-loan order; AWG 15% and its preemption of state law; tax levies kept out; how state limits are handled

evidence.correctness: Exercised calc.mjs with node -e. Single-order outputs recompute by hand from 15 U.S.C. 1673 and DOL Fact Sheet #30: weekly floor 30 x 7.25 = 217.50, biweekly 435, semimonthly 471.25, monthly 942.50 (protectedFloor); weekly $250 disposable -> $32.50 (excess over floor, FS30 middle band); $370 -> $92.50 (25%, FS30 example); $217.50 -> $0; biweekly $580 -> $145 (FS30 biweekly example); semimonthly $600 -> $128.75; monthly $1,200 -> $257.50; support $1,000 at 55/65% -> $550/$650; AWG $1,000 -> $150, $230 -> $12.50 (lesser of 15% or excess over floor, 31 CFR 285.11(i)(2)); sample stub disposable 2000-443 = 1,557, cap 25% = 389.25; what-if +$300 at 25% tax keeps 300-75-56.25 = 168.75. All match. But the combined rule is wrong: Fact Sheet #30's own example (weekly disposable $370, $140 already withheld for child support, then a consumer-debt order) says no ordinary garnishment may be made because support already exceeds 25%; the tool allows $45.00 more (total $185). calc.mjs:165 caps ordinary debt at min(25% - nonSupportUsed, supportCap - support), so support never counts against the 25%. Same for a student loan after support: 31 CFR 285.11(i)(3) gives the lesser of 15% or 25% minus amounts withheld under priority orders; $1,000 disposable with $200 support gives $50, the tool gives $150. A wrong number on the case payroll sees most often (support plus a creditor), so 2.
evidence.completeness: README and VENTURE.yaml features checked: disposable earnings, ordinary/student/support caps, pay-period floors, up to three orders with support-first ordering, stub check (above max, below max, matches), order-asks-more finding, at-or-below-floor finding, voluntary-deduction note, state percent box, overtime what-if, draft letter, CSV download, usage counting with opt-out and DNT. All present and run end to end through analyze/whatIf/requestLetter/reportCsv; no TODOs or stubs. served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder origin. The combined-cap feature exists but applies the wrong rule (see correctness).
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 40 pass, 0 fail, 0.12 s. Five seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: semimonthly weeks 65/30 -> 2 caught; arrears +5 -> +0 caught; belowFloor <= -> < caught; floor excess +1 cent caught; student-loan cap's 25%-minus-ordinary term removed SURVIVED. 4 of 5 caught. Worse, calc.test.mjs:65-71 pins the wrong combined rule (support $300 then ordinary $111.75 on $823.50 disposable; FS30 gives $0), so the suite would fail a correct fix. No test is taken from Fact Sheet #30's worked examples.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (339 lines), index.html script, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Whole-cent arithmetic, one engine shared by page, letter and CSV, parseMoney rejects ambiguous shapes, errors are messages not silent defaults. Defects: the 'questioned' total sums unlike quantities (over-withholding and the unpaid balance an order asks for) at calc.mjs:243; yearlyTake float multiply without rounding (calc.mjs:191); state cap branch for student loans (calc.mjs:169). Acceptable for a static tool.
evidence.claims: Checked: floor table $217.50/$435/$471.25/$942.50 (backed, recomputed); 25%/15%/50-65% (backed); 'Student loan and ordinary debt garnishments together are limited to 25%' (backed by code, incomplete: support also counts); FAQ 'All garnishments together cannot exceed the support percentage' (true but omits that a creditor gets nothing once support reaches 25%, index.html:146); 'applies the combined caps' (VENTURE.yaml) implemented with the wrong rule; 'most that is in question over a year' tile shows $7,839 for the sample stub while the over-withholding is $90.75 x 26 = $2,359.50, because it adds the order's unpaid balance ($210.75 x 26) that is not taken from the worker (calc.mjs:243, index.html:213); 'nothing is uploaded' backed (no fetch/XHR/beacon, enforced by page.test.mjs:47); disclaimer, no-warranty, independence and an honest 'Unverified' note present on index and README.
evidence.fitness: A worker with one ordinary-debt or one support order gets a right cap and a sensible letter to payroll. A payroll specialist cannot use it for the cases they actually work: multiple orders where support is in place (wrong answer), state rules beyond a single percent (no state floor multiplier such as a state minimum wage x 40 or 50, no head-of-household exemption, no state that bars ordinary garnishment except by typing 0), federal and state tax levies (Pub 1494 exempt amount) not modelled, Chapter 13 not modelled. Stated limits cover the last two.
evidence.domain: Disposable earnings definition, floor multiples (29 CFR 870.10 via FS30), support percentages and AWG floor match the sources. Departures: support withholding not counted toward the 25% limit for later ordinary/AWG orders (FS30 example; 31 CFR 285.11(i)(3)); a typed state limit is applied to federal student-loan AWG, which 20 U.S.C. 1095a(a) and 31 CFR 285.11 apply 'notwithstanding any provision of State law' (state 10% gives $100 instead of $150); state handling is percent-only.

defects.what: Support withheld first is not counted against the 25% limit for a later ordinary-debt order. DOL Fact Sheet #30's own example (weekly disposable $370, $140 support) allows no consumer-debt garnishment; the tool allows $45 more (total $185). Ordinary cap should be max(0, min(25%, excess over floor) - support taken - student taken)
Same for a student-loan AWG after support: 31 CFR 285.11(i)(3) caps it at the lesser of 15% or 25% minus priority withholding; $1,000 disposable with $200 support gives $50, the tool $150

The test pins the wrong combined rule (support $300 then ordinary $111.75 on $823.50 disposable; FS30 gives $0), and no test uses Fact Sheet #30's worked examples; mutant removing the student-plus-ordinary 25% term survived
'Most that is in question over a year' adds the unpaid balance an order asks for (not taken from the worker) to the over-withholding: sample stub shows $7,839 where over-withholding is $2,359.50
A typed state percent is applied to federal student-loan AWG, which applies notwithstanding state law (20 U.S.C. 1095a(a)); state 10% shows $100 instead of $150
State law handled only as one percent: no state floor multiplier or state minimum wage basis (multiplier fixed at 30), no head-of-household exemption; tax levies not modelled (stated)
Support FAQ says only that all garnishments stay within the support percentage; omits that a creditor or AWG order gets nothing once support reaches 25%

verdict: A careful, honest single-order calculator: the pay-period floors ($217.50/$435/$471.25/$942.50), the 25%-or-excess rule (FS30's $250, $370 and $580 examples), the 55/65% support caps, the AWG 15%-or-excess rule and the overtime what-if all recompute by hand, the disclaimer and 'unverified' note are present, and 4 of 5 seeded bugs are caught. But the combined-order rule, which VENTURE.yaml names as what makes it more than a calculator, is wrong: support already withheld is not counted against the 25% limit, so on DOL Fact Sheet #30's own example it allows $45 of consumer-debt garnishment where the DOL says none, and an AWG after support gets $150 where 31 CFR 285.11(i)(3) gives $50. A unit test pins the wrong rule. The 'in question' tile triples the over-withholding on the sample stub, and a state percent is wrongly applied to federal AWG. Correctness, verification and claims are 2: does not meet the bar; finished (completeness 3).
